content: 1. Digoxin levels or effects are increased by erythromycin stearate through inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Both esmolol and digoxin elevate serum potassium levels. Esmolol enhances the effects of digoxin via pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to enhanced bradycardia. Use caution and monitor. 3. Esomeprazole increases digoxin toxicity through mechanisms related to prolonged proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use, which may cause hypomagnesemia and elevate the risk of digoxin toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 4. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while ethacrynic acid decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear, but ethacrynic acid enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. Hypokalemia increases digoxin effects. Use caution and monitor. 5. Etodolac and digoxin both increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 6. Etravirine increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 7. Ezogabine raises digoxin levels by reducing renal clearance, possibly through inhibition of renal tubular secretion by its active metabolite NAMR. Monitor digoxin levels closely. 8. Famciclovir increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism, raising digoxin Cmax by approximately 19%. Use caution and monitor. 9. Felodipine increases digoxin levels or effects via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 10. Both fenoprofen and digoxin elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 11. Ferric maltol and digoxin may mutually increase each other’s levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may reduce the bioavailability of either drug. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Separate administration of ferric maltol and certain oral drugs may be necessary. 12. Fleroxacin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 13. Flibanserin increases digoxin levels via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Increased monitoring of drugs transported by P-gp with a narrow therapeutic index is recommended. Use caution and monitor. 14. Both flurbiprofen and digoxin elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor. 15. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while formoterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 16. Fosfomycin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 17. Fosinopril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Fostamatinib increases digoxin levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs and consider dosage reduction when co-administered. 20. Fostemsavir increases digoxin levels or effects by inhibiting the OATP1B1/3 transporter. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. Monitor closely. 21. Digoxin increases serum potassium, while furosemide decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear. Furosemide enhances digoxin effects via pharmacodynamic synergy. Hypokalemia increases digoxin effects. Use caution and monitor. 22. Gemifloxacin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 23. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor. 24. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases digoxin levels or effects via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating therapy. Reduce digoxin dose by approximately 50% or adjust dosing frequency as needed. Monitor closely. 25.
